fixes.explanation: Yes, baker, that's the one. The writer says, "And this is the promise that He Himself made to us: eternal life." It's a promise that comes from Him, and the writer counts himself in with the believers when he says "to us." That's worth saying LOUD: ETERNAL LIFE (1 John 2:25)!

Nothing about a capture here, friend. The writer says the believers heard the antichrist is coming, and then he says "…now many antichrists have appeared." So the news is not one figure caught, it's many who have shown up (1 John 2:18).

Some is too small, friend. The writer says, "You, however, have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know the truth." Some? SOME?! That shrinks the whole batch down to a handful, when he's talking about every one of them. And notice where that anointing comes from: the Holy One (1 John 2:20).
Not this time, baker. The writer says he wrote "…because no lie comes from the truth." So no lie comes out of the truth. The card says a lie can, so it's false (1 John 2:21).

That's right, baker. The writer says, "Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, but whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well." So the one who denies the Son does not have the Father. The one who confesses the Son has the Father as well (1 John 2:23).

A land was promised to Abraham, the man God called out of his homeland, and to his family (Genesis 12:1, 7). But that's not the promise in this verse. The writer says, "And this is the promise that He Himself made to us: eternal life." So the answer here is eternal life, friend (1 John 2:25).
